questions.explanation: Mass flow rate of air through nozzle = mass entering nozzle = mass exit from nozzle [latex] \begin{aligned} m &=\rho_{i} A_{i} V_{i}=\rho_{e} A_{e} V_{e} \\ \text { where } & i=\text { inlet } \\ e &=\text { exit } \\ \rho &=\text { density } \\ A &=\text { Area } \\ V &=\text { velocity } \\ p &=\rho R T \\ m &=\frac{A_{e} V_{e} p_{e}}{R T_{e}}\\ \text{Given }R&=0.287 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ p_{e}&=50 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}[/latex] For isentropic process [latex] \begin{array}{l} \left(\frac{T_{e}}{T_{i}}\right)=\left(\frac{p_{e}}{p_{i}}\right)^{\gamma-1 / \gamma} \\ \frac{T_{e}}{400}=\left(\frac{50}{500}\right)^{0.4 / 1.4}\\ \text{or}\quad T_{e}=239.73 \mathrm{K} \end{array}[/latex] Mass flow rate, [latex] m=\frac{50 \times 0.005 \times V_{e}}{0.287 \times 239.73} \qquad \cdots(1)[/latex] Using steady flow energy equation [latex] \begin{aligned} h_{i}+\frac{V_{i}^{2}}{2}+q&=h_{e}+\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2}+w\\ \text{where }\quad V_{i}&=0 \\ q&=0 \quad \text{adiabatic flow}\\ w &=0 \\ \therefore \quad h_{i} &=h_{e}+\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2} \end{aligned}[/latex] On units balancing, we get [latex] \begin{aligned} h_{i} &=h_{e}+\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2000} \\ \text{or}\quad h_{i}-h_{e} &=\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2000}\\ c_{p}\left(T_{i}-T_{e}\right)&=\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2000}\\ 1 \times(400-239.73)&=\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2000} \\ V_{e}&=567.57 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex] From Eq. (1), we get [latex] m=\frac{50 \times 0.005 \times 567.57}{0.287 \times 239.73}[/latex] [latex] =2.06 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Mass flow rate of air through nozzle
= mass entering nozzle
= mass exit from nozzle
[latex] \begin{aligned} m &=\rho_{i} A_{i} V_{i}=\rho_{e} A_{e} V_{e} \\ \text { where } & i=\text { inlet } \\ e &=\text { exit } \\ \rho &=\text { density } \\ A &=\text { Area } \\ V &=\text { velocity } \\ p &=\rho R T \\ m &=\frac{A_{e} V_{e} p_{e}}{R T_{e}}\\ \text{Given }R&=0.287 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ p_{e}&=50 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For isentropic process
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \left(\frac{T_{e}}{T_{i}}\right)=\left(\frac{p_{e}}{p_{i}}\right)^{\gamma-1 / \gamma} \\ \frac{T_{e}}{400}=\left(\frac{50}{500}\right)^{0.4 / 1.4}\\ \text{or}\quad T_{e}=239.73 \mathrm{K} \end{array}[/latex]
Mass flow rate,
[latex] m=\frac{50 \times 0.005 \times V_{e}}{0.287 \times 239.73} \qquad \cdots(1)[/latex]
Using steady flow energy equation
[latex] \begin{aligned} h_{i}+\frac{V_{i}^{2}}{2}+q&=h_{e}+\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2}+w\\ \text{where }\quad V_{i}&=0 \\ q&=0 \quad \text{adiabatic flow}\\ w &=0 \\ \therefore \quad h_{i} &=h_{e}+\frac{V_{e}^{2}}{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
On units balancing, we get

From Eq. (1), we get
[latex] m=\frac{50 \times 0.005 \times 567.57}{0.287 \times 239.73}[/latex]
[latex] =2.06 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}[/latex]
